44, Crystal Selection in Radio Transmitter T-
       416/GR

   Before the transmitter can be operated, the
operating frequency must be determined and the
transmitter must be tuned for that operating

frequency. However, before the tuning pro-

cedure can be carried out, the following prelimi-
nary steps must be performed:

a. Release the transmitter from Electrical

Equipment Cabinet CY—1221(*)/G by turning the

hold-in lock handle counterclockwise. The trans-

mitter then may be pulled out of the equipment
cabinet by the handle located on the front panel.

b. Remove the right and left side dust covers

from the transmitter; be sure that all tubes are

in place (fig. 21).

c. When determining the correct crystal fre-

quency, bear in mind that the two preset operating

frequencies of the transmitter must not differ

by more than 1 mc. After selecting two oper-

ating frequencies that meet this requirement,

choose the correct crystal frequency by means of

the following formula:

                        Ad  :
crystal frequency= eens requency (kc)

Example:
      F,=desired operating frequency=162 me.

      F,=alternative operating frequency=161 me.
      X,=crystal frequency required for F;.
      X,=crystal frequency required for F%.

    X=mr35 1—62gq,00—0k.e=5062.500 ke.

    X=_ 5Fy91>61,g0p007_75031.250 ke.

   d. To maintain accuracy of the operating fre-    Figure 34.                                             TM 804-31
quency, carry division out to three places to the               Transmitter crystal oven, exploded view.
right of the decimal point. The above example
shows the maximum allowable frequency differ-                                                                 39
ence between the two operating frequencies.
Actually, more efficient transmitter operation is
attained when the two frequencies chosen are
closer together. ‘ See paragraph 43.

   e. Install the required crystals as shown in
figure 34. To do this, first unplug the entire
crystal oven assembly E401. Remove the three
screws securing the cover of the crystal oven to
the socket, unplug the heater and thermostat
element from the socket, and then insert the
crystals into the socket base. Reassemble in the
reverse order.

                                       CHAPTER 6
                      FIELD MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS

       Note. This chapter contains information for field maintenance. The amount of repair that can be performed by
units having field maintenance responsibilities is limited by the tools and test equipment available and by the skill of the
repairman.

Section |. TROUBLESHOOTING AT FIELD MAINTENANCE LEVEL

      Warning: There are certain points in the radio set that operate at 500 volts; therefore, when servic-
ing the radio set, be extremely careful of exposure to high-voltage points. Be sure that all power is turned
off before touching any of the connections. Short out the filter capacitors in Power Supply PP-804/U.
Read the caution notices on the components and in their respective instruction books before attempting
repairs.
